turns.content: A synthesized small peptide has two nearby proton-NMR peaks for one alpha proton; their equal integrals sum to 1H, and spin-spin splitting has been excluded. What does this suggest about the sample? The measurements are achiral, and no direct formation-mechanism evidence is available.
At elevated temperature, achiral LC-MS gives two equal-intensity peaks with identical mass spectra matching the expected compound. What does that add to the interpretation?
Why can these achiral measurements distinguish many diastereomers but not normally a pair of enantiomers?
Classify the two observed forms and explain, using only the NMR and LC-MS evidence, why precursor contamination or double coupling fits less well.
Check whether the two observed features are consistent with that classification.
How strong is the assignment, and what remains uncertain about the exact stereochemical relation and how it formed?
What follow-up separation, derivatization, or isolated-fraction measurement would be most useful to test this assignment further?
State the best-supported classification and origin hypothesis, with an appropriate confidence level.
